clue.text: Self-centred travel in troubled cities

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disordered, so the next word's letters are rearranged
one piece is placed inside the other, sitting within it

blocks.note: to travel is to go
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed traveller roams through cities in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled cities' reads as a scene, but troubled works on the letters of cities alone, and the travel word then sits after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoistic person thinks mainly of themselves, which is what self-centred describes; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: With beat raised, dance that's hit on course

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to beat is to flog
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A rhythm is pumped up and a dance gets going, hit on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a golf course, not a course of a meal or a study.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf ball is the small dimpled sphere players strike with clubs around a golf course.

clue.text: Reinstate cop, possibly in officer's post

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the preceding letters can be reordered

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A suspended policeman might be restored to his post.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is the office or rank held by an inspector, an officer of police.

clue.text: Passionate little heroine switching ends

indicators.note: the first and last letters trade places with each other while the middle stays put

blocks.note: Little Dorrit is the heroine of the Dickens novel of that name

explanation.surface: A small romantic heroine turns out to be quite fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' belongs to the name: Amy Dorrit is Dickens's Little Dorrit. Swap her D and T to get TORRID.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid is used of an intensely passionate love affair, so the words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Something baked, a piece of which is like pie

definitions.text: a piece of which is like pie

blocks.note: first meaning: a sweet baked item

blocks.clueFragment: a piece of which is like pie
blocks.note: second meaning: 'a piece of ___' is a task as easy as pie

explanation.walkthrough: The second half points to two idioms: 'a piece of cake' and 'easy as pie' both mean something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake is a baked food, and the idiom 'piece of cake' means as easy as pie.

clue.text: Time in European city with an enthusiastic supporter

indicators.note: the letter for time is set within the city's name

blocks.note: the capital of France
T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spending time in a continental city with a keen fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a strong, often uncritical adherent of a cause or party, a committed backer.

clue.text: Clobber that's often worn with pants

blocks.note: first meaning: to hit hard
second meaning: a strap round the waist holding up trousers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is also British slang for clothes, which makes it look like a garment; here it is the verb meaning hit. Pants are trousers in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt someone is to hit them, and a belt is the strap commonly fastened around trouser waists.

clue.text: Like man dealing with issue in caring way

blocks.note: first meaning: issue is offspring, so a man dealing with his children acts like a parent
second meaning: kindly and protective

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem to deal with, but it is the old legal word for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherly describes the behaviour of a parent towards children, protective and kind, hence caring.

clue.text: What's detested in every article, mother concludes

indicators.note: this word says the parent comes last, finishing off the string of pieces

blocks.note: English has three articles: an, a and the; every one of them is used
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother objects to something hateful in every piece she reads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical kind, and all three English ones appear in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something or someone intensely loathed, so it names a thing that is detested.

clue.text: Letters regularly falling out of mailbags, unfortunately

indicators.note: letters dropping out at regular intervals means every other one is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A postal mishap: letters spilling from the sacks, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection expressing regret or sorrow, used much as 'sadly' or 'unfortunately' is.

clue.text: Ideal speech for selling musical gift

blocks.note: ideal means perfect
a sales pitch is a talk meant to persuade a buyer

explanation.surface: The ideal patter for a salesman pushing a musical present.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect pitch is the rare talent of naming or singing any note without a reference, an innate musical ability.

clue.text: Very poor current politician on left I drop

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
Member of Parliament
as in food left over, remaining
taken as written
to shed is to let fall, as with leaves

explanation.surface: A broke left-wing politician of today talks of dropping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not the political side but what remains, as in 'any left over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impoverished means reduced to poverty, without money, which matches very poor.

clue.text: Home guard who'd act when disturbed? Good

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order and resettled differently

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, apostrophe ignored
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A member of the Home Guard springs into action when roused, which is good.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's wartime volunteer militia; here 'home guard' is just a dog protecting the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a dog kept to guard a house against intruders, a domestic sentry.

clue.text: Imposing old relative briefly on daughter

blocks.note: gran is the short form of grandmother
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A grandmother briefly imposes herself on her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand describes something large and impressive in appearance, so it is a synonym of imposing.

clue.text: Pressure to divide excellent meal

indicators.note: a letter dividing a word splits it apart by sitting between its letters

blocks.note: super means excellent
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure to share out a fine dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, often a light one, so it is a kind of meal.

clue.text: Starts off aria like true opera singer

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, one taken from each following word

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An opera singer begins an aria in authentic operatic style.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the lower female or high male voice range, so is a type of singer.

clue.text: Music for church service

blocks.note: an air is a tune
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Choosing hymns for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a church service; it is one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The air force is one of the armed services, the military branch fighting in the air.

clue.text: Isn't perturbed about a bad mark

indicators.note: perturbed means thrown into disorder, so the word's letters are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to jumble, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is unbothered about getting a poor grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a discoloured blemish or, figuratively, a blot on a reputation: a bad mark either way.

clue.text: Beneficial having union after rise in pay

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that has risen is read upwards, so backwards
the turned piece is placed inside the word for pay

blocks.note: TU is a trade union
a salary is regular pay

explanation.surface: A union deal after a pay rise is good for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Salutary means producing a good effect, often after something unpleasant, so it is close to beneficial.

clue.text: Take part in everything that's jolly

indicators.note: taking part of a word means lifting a run of its letters from inside it

blocks.note: the letters from second to fifth

explanation.surface: Joining in all the fun that's merry.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'jolly' can be an adverb meaning very, as in 'jolly good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly is informal British for very, as in 'jolly well done', an intensifying adverb.

clue.text: Check son getting into coach again

indicators.note: one item getting into another ends up enclosed inside it

blocks.note: to train once more
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father checks whether his son is boarding the bus again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus but is the verb train.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check, so the verb check is a synonym.

clue.text: Don't forget about ring

blocks.note: re means concerning
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A reminder to remember about phoning someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to remember, which is the positive way of saying not to forget.

clue.text: Is imprisoned by key and lock, suffering

indicators.note: something imprisoned is held between walls, so it sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: D is a musical key
taken as written
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A prisoner held under key and lock is in misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key and lock' reads as security, but they are a musical key and a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is severe anxiety or pain, so it means suffering.

clue.text: Small shack for tool

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hovel is a crude dwelling

explanation.surface: A little garden shed to keep implements in.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a broad-bladed digging implement, a common garden tool.

clue.text: Weird state in US, too fond of self-display

indicators.note: weird signals strangeness, so the following letters take an odd new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange American state that likes to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentatious describes a showy person or thing designed to impress, someone keen on flaunting.

clue.text: Explosive stuff about drug that's secured by guys

indicators.note: about means around, so the explosive surrounds the drug letter

blocks.note: trinitrotoluene, the explosive
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Bomb-makers with narcotics are guarded by some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' are not men but guy ropes, the lines pegged out to hold up canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is held upright by guy ropes staked into the ground, so it is secured by guys.

clue.text: What changed as result of spring coming?

indicators.note: changed letters are altered in order, giving a different arrangement

blocks.note: the four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question about what altered when the season turned.
explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like a riddle with no wordplay, but its first word is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw is the melting of ice and snow that follows when spring arrives after winter.

clue.text: Cape that's over one's shoulders

blocks.note: first meaning: a headland jutting into the sea
second meaning: the body part sitting on top of the shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: A cape is also a garment worn over the shoulders, which makes the clue look like one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a promontory, as in Beachy Head, and is also what sits above a person's shoulders.

clue.text: Is permitted to do wrong in airline, producing capital

indicators.note: the word for doing wrong goes inside the airline's initials

blocks.note: one who can is allowed to
British Airways
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: An airline staffer allowed to misbehave on board makes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' hints at money but is a capital city; BA is British Airways.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the capital city of Australia.

clue.text: Opposite of rare statement of approval

blocks.note: first meaning: steak cooked right through
second meaning: congratulations on a job done

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' suggests scarce, so the opposite would be common; it is rare meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-done meat is fully cooked, unlike rare, and 'Well done!' is a cry of praise.
